interface.title: StemCell Fate Explorer
interface.stage_of_work: Exploring and interpreting results from an analysis that has already been run (CellRank/Scanpy/GPCCA outputs are precomputed)
interface.what_it_is_for: Browsing a human CD34+ bone-marrow single-cell atlas to look at CellRank fate probabilities for each terminal fate, putative driver genes for each lineage, marker-gene expression across pseudotime, and the analysis provenance.

data.note: The processed outputs ship with the app: 5,780 cells, 14,041 genes, 10 annotated cell states and 6 terminal fates (Mono_1, DCs_1, Mega, DCs_2, Ery_2, CLP). Nothing is uploaded and no analysis is rerun. Files I exported: Ery_2_putative_driver_genes.csv (15 rows, set by the slider), Mega_putative_driver_genes.csv (60 rows) and umap-cell-state.png. A copy icon in the Methods JSON viewer was clicked, but the clipboard contents were never confirmed.

screens_never_reached: Regenerate analysis outputs (scripts/prepare_data.py): not exposed in the UI, and the brief said not to run it
not_done: The built-in 'Download as CSV' icon on the Fate Map summary table produced no download file in this headless browser. The page's own 'Download selected driver genes (CSV)' button did work
A single click on a legend entry to add a second cluster (Mono_2) after isolating Mono_1 produced no visible change, so I did not confirm legend toggling in single-click mode

There is no quantitative early-versus-late commitment comparison along pseudotime (for example, fate probability plotted against pseudotime). I judged it visually from the fate maps and the per-state means only
Gene Explorer offers only 12 curated markers, so arbitrary genes such as the drivers AZU1 or GP9 cannot be plotted there
View selections are not kept when switching views (for example, Fate Map went back to Mono_1/UMAP), so comparing views means reselecting each time
